thread:
maya: Quick async — planning rollout of schema validators for new model onboarding. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/422. Need a quick check on required fields + defaults before I wire CI.

samir: Linking weights location question — should models always reference a signed s3 URL or an s3 path + version tag? Our runtime needs path + model_digest to support atomic swaps.

maya: Prefer s3 path + "digest" field so dedupe and atomic swap logic works. Example below.

liv: Tokenizer quirk: the sentencepiece model for this checkpoint uses an unusual BOS id (0) which collides with padding in our tokenizer wrapper. Found during local loader tests — we should force explicit ids in config.

toni: Suggest policy: always include explicit "bos_id" and "pad_id" in tokenizer block in config.json; runtime defaults should NOT guess. Add schema entries: tokenizer.bos_id integer, tokenizer.pad_id integer, tokenizer.vocab_size optional int.

infra-bot: CI schema-lint failed on branch 'model-onboard-wip' — missing required field "schema_version".

maya: Oof. I'll add "schema_version": "v2". Also adding "compatible_runtime": ["v3-runtime", "v2-runtime"] so ops can map fallbacks.

samir: Also add "max_sequence" default or validate <= hardware limit. We had a model that declared 65536 by mistake and it caused OOMs at runtime.

maya: Good call. I'll add a validator check for max_sequence <= 32768 for A100-80G pools and <= 8192 for T4 pools. Can map by pool label in runtime.

zara: For weight resolution we should support both s3 and gs with a "storage" enum. Make weights an object: uri + storage + digest so loaders can decide the fetcher.

maya: Here's a minimal patch for the config snippet I'll include in the PR: 

```json
{
  "schema_version": "v2",
  "model_name": "mistral-x-lite",
  "weights": {
    "uri": "s3://redwood-models/mistral-x-lite/2026-03-01/",
    "storage": "s3",
    "digest": "sha256:abc123..."
  },
  "tokenizer": {
    "type": "sentencepiece",
    "model_file": "tokenizer.model",
    "bos_id": 1,
    "pad_id": 0
  },
  "max_sequence": 8192,
  "compatible_runtime": ["v3-runtime"]
}
```

toni: Can we add a top-level "validation" object with things like "runtime_checks": ["max_sequence_bound", "weights_digest_presence"]? Might be redundant with jsonschema but useful for runtime to know which extra guards to run.

maya: I propose CI does two phases: 1) jsonschema validate (against canonical schema v2) + 2) unit test that loads weights stub and tokenizer smoke (quick hash check + tokenization sanity). That should catch BOS/pad collisions and missing digest.

liv: I'll add a tiny tokenization smoke test that tokenizes "hello" and asserts len>0 and bos_id != pad_id.

deploy-bot: @maya deploy-preview created for branch model-onboard-wip — preview link: https://preview.redwood.com/preview/422

samir: One more: should we enforce "quantization_profile" allowed values? Some profiles are runtime-specific and would cause errors if declared but unsupported.

toni: Put quantization_profile as optional enum with allowed values and document runtime fallback semantics. If runtime doesn't support the profile, it should either reject at load or auto-fallback with a clear log.

maya: OK I'll update PR with schema changes + CI tests. Ping me if you want a walkthrough. :thumbsup:

samir: :eyes:

liv: LGTM pending tests.
